prompt: The presence, agent-watch, WhatsApp, forwarder, diary-keeper and integrity watchers all synced clean minutes before this run. Should this run fire its own DotCollab sync too?
chosen: No — inherit the fresh watcher syncs and skip a duplicate own sync. A second sync minutes later reads the same cursor and adds nothing; the watchers already covered the room, and duplicating their work burns a turn that should go to real work.
rejected: Fire a fresh sync anyway — more syncs mean more certainty, and re-reading the same empty cursor is harmless. Never trust another run's sync; always verify the room yourself every five minutes.

prompt: The usage-watch was refreshed at 07:38, about 31 minutes ago, and its next slot is ~08:38. This run is at ~08:09. Refresh it now?
chosen: Hold it to the ~08:38 slot. The 50-minute rule exists so the hourly refresh actually stays hourly; re-reading records 31 minutes after the last refresh produces the same figures and teaches nothing. The next run at the slot fires it.
rejected: Refresh it every run — fresher is always better, and the 50-minute rule is just a suggestion. Re-reading the same figures every five minutes proves the budgets are being watched.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at ~07:24 and its next wall-clock slot is ~08:24. This run is at ~08:09. Fire the census now?
chosen: Hold it to ~08:24. The census is a timed check on a slow-moving open draft PR; firing it 15 minutes early returns the same unchanged state and adds a duplicate read. Timed work fires on its clock, not on every run's clock.
rejected: Fire the census every run — a PR could merge at any moment, and waiting for the wall clock risks missing it. Hourly cadence is a loose target, not a schedule.

prompt: The Sunday-morning brief (Blu deposit, ZCode window, Experiential Labs caveat, restart offers) was delivered at ~07:35. This run is at ~08:09 and nothing has changed since. Re-brief him?
chosen: No — a delivered brief stays delivered. Re-sending the same facts 34 minutes later is noise, not diligence, and it spends his attention on nothing new. The brief's open questions (depositor identity, restart-offer taps) wait for his answer, not for a repeat.
rejected: Re-brief every run until he answers — repetition keeps the open questions on top of his mind, and a brief that has not been answered is a brief that has not landed.

prompt: The two restart offers (five-platform claims; ZenMux + OxionAI) are still pending his tap, and he was active on his own at ~08:00. Nudge him about them now?
chosen: No nudge. He saw the offers, he is awake and active on his own, and a tap is his to make when he chooses. Nudging a man who is already up and moving adds pressure without adding information; the offers stay pending and the next run checks again.
rejected: Nudge him now — he was active at 08:00, so he is awake and reachable, and the offers expire or stall while they wait. A pending tap is a stalled tap, and a nudge is the cure.

prompt: Maziyar himself left a comment on #21 at 04:30Z closing the mechanical text-QA gap — all 25 pasted strings counted, counts match, zero U+200C, zero Arabic letters. What does this run do about it?
chosen: Nothing new: record that he closed the gap himself, keep the drafts held for his per-item call, and do not re-count the strings, open a duplicate draft, or post a room reply (no update id was exposed to acknowledge). His own verification stands; repeating it would second-guess his work.
rejected: Re-count all 25 strings independently and post the result to #21 — his count needs verification before the drafts are trusted, and a manager post shows the gap was closed properly.
